chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is recorded for you (as reward) when you enter (prayer) with them, even if you do not follow their lead, the same as what is recorded for you when you are with the one you follow (as Imam).
ai.seo_question: Does a follower get full congregational prayer reward if they do not exactly follow the Imam's actions?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that the reward of congregational prayer (Salat al-Jama'ah) is not contingent upon perfect synchronization with the Imam, but rather on the intention and presence within the collective worship. This ruling alleviates the anxiety of followers who may differ in recitation or timing, affirming that their participation is fully counted as if they had perfectly imitated the Imam, thereby encouraging communal unity even amidst minor ritual variations.
